senses.sense_definition: The act of moving something from its original or proper place.

examples.text: The war caused the mass <w>displacement</w> of thousands of innocent civilians.
The <w>displacement</w> of the old furniture made the room feel much larger.

senses.sense_definition: A measurement of the distance and direction of an object from a starting point.

examples.text: In physics, <w>displacement</w> is a vector quantity that includes both magnitude and direction.
The total <w>displacement</w> of the car was zero because it returned to its start.

senses.sense_definition: The total volume of all cylinders in an internal combustion engine.

examples.text: The sports car features a powerful engine with a large <w>displacement</w> for better performance.
Engine <w>displacement</w> is typically measured in liters or cubic centimeters.

senses.sense_definition: The weight of the water that a ship pushes aside when it floats.

examples.text: The massive tanker has a total <w>displacement</w> of over fifty thousand tons.
Naval architects calculate the <w>displacement</w> to ensure the vessel remains stable at sea.

senses.sense_definition: The psychological act of transferring emotions from the intended person to a safer target.

examples.text: His anger at his boss was a clear case of <w>displacement</w> when he yelled at his dog.
Psychologists often identify <w>displacement</w> as a common defense mechanism in stressful situations.
